tr.td: SQL injection attempt in password field
Input sanitization, no server error exposure
Valid login → Logout → Browser close → Cookie persistence check

div.strong: Phase 1: Test Case Design (RICE POT Analysis)

div.div: 1. Create JIRA Test Issues (Issue Type: Test) for TC-01 through TC-05
2. Link tests to Story: VWO-LOGIN-001 (if exists, else create stub)
3. Set Labels: automation, playwright, login-regression, rice-pot
4. Export test steps to JIRA Test Manager with Gherkin syntax (Given/When/Then)
TC-01, TC-02, TC-03, TC-05: Must PASS (assert true)
On failure: Trigger page.screenshot({ path: 'bugs/TC-04-security-fail.png', fullPage: true })
Capture page.url() and console.errors() logs
TC-04 (SQL Injection): Must FAIL intentionally (assert expected security block, but simulate bug by expecting success)
PASS: Attach HTML report fragment + success screenshot to JIRA Test Execution
Summary: [AUTO] Login Security: TC-04 Input Sanitization Failure
Description: Expected vs Actual behavior, Steps to Reproduce, Environment details, Screenshot attachment
Link to parent Test Case (TC-04)
Priority: High
Component: Authentication Security
FAIL: Auto-create JIRA Bug (Issue Type: Bug) with:
I — Instructions (Phased Execution)
Single Page Application (SPA) post-login
Multi-language support (i18n)
Cookie-based session management with "Remember Me" persistence
CSRF token validation on login POST
UTF-8 character handling in international locales
Session fixation vulnerabilities
Client-side validation bypass
